data.description:
# The shared webhook/rerun secret is written to journald in every access-log line

## Context / Problem

The review-bot receiver is a uvicorn app, and uvicorn's default access log records the full
request line INCLUDING THE QUERY STRING. Both authenticated endpoints take their secret as a
QUERY PARAMETER (`?token=...`), so every request writes the secret to stderr -> journald in
clear text:

    INFO:  127.0.0.1:34184 - "POST /rerun?token=<the actual secret>&change=1323 HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted
    INFO:  172.21.0.4:33070 - "POST /webhook?token=<the actual secret> HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted

Observed directly in the production container's journal (`journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1`).

## Why it matters

* **The secret is the auth for both endpoints.** `config.py:239` is
  `webhook_token = os.environ.get("WEBHOOK_TOKEN", "").strip() or bot_token`, and this
  container sets no `WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, so the webhook token IS `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` — the
  review bot's Gerrit credential. Anything that can read the journal therefore learns a
  credential that can both drive reviews AND act as the bot against Gerrit.
* **The blast radius is wider than the box.** journald content flows into anything that reads
  it: `infra/scripts/observability.sh` greps the same journal, operators paste log excerpts into
  tickets and chat, and any future log-shipping would carry the secret off-host. It also means
  the secret cannot be treated as unexposed after any incident that involved sharing logs.
* **It is a fail-open exposure, not a fail-closed one:** nothing errors, nothing alarms, and the
  endpoint keeps working — so there is no signal that would ever surface it.

DISCOVERED the hard way: an agent grepping the journal for `/rerun` activity while working
[rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] surfaced the token into a session transcript. That is the failure mode
— the secret is sitting in the most-grepped log on the box.

**This ticket does not fix the exposure that already happened.** The token in the journal (and
anywhere journal excerpts have been shared) must be treated as compromised and ROTATED
independently of the code fix. Rotation alone is also not sufficient: without the fix, the new
token is logged the moment it is first used.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — the `/webhook` and `/rerun` handlers and/or the uvicorn
  logging configuration (`configure_logging`).
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — the `uvicorn` invocation, if the access-log format or
  its disabling belongs there.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the `/rerun` recipe currently instructs the operator to
  put the token in a URL, which is what puts it in the log; and a rotation note.

## Approach (options, with the tradeoff stated)

1. **Move the secret out of the query string** — accept it as a header (e.g. `X-Rebar-Token`) or
   in the POST body. Cleanest: access logs record the request line, not headers. But
   `/webhook` is called BY GERRIT, so the Gerrit-side webhook configuration must be able to
   send it — check what the `webhook` plugin supports before assuming a header is expressible.
   `/rerun` is operator-driven and can move to a header immediately regardless.
2. **Scrub the access log** — install a uvicorn log filter that redacts `token=[^&]*`. Keeps the
   URL shape, protects the value, and covers BOTH endpoints even if Gerrit cannot send a header.
   Weaker in principle (the secret still transits a URL, so it can leak via any other component
   that logs URLs) but it is the only option that works without a Gerrit-side change.
3. Do both: header for `/rerun`, redaction filter as the backstop for `/webhook`.

Do NOT simply disable the access log — it is load-bearing for debugging and for the
`observability.sh` greps.

## Testing

The oracle must assert on the EMITTED LOG LINE, not on the handler's behaviour, because the
handler is already correct — it is the logging that leaks:

- drive a request carrying a known sentinel token through the app with `caplog` (or a captured
  uvicorn handler) and assert the sentinel does NOT appear in any emitted record, while the
  route and status DO;
- verify RED by reverting the fix and observing the sentinel reappear;
- if a header is adopted, a second test that a query-string token is REJECTED (or at least not
  logged), so the old path cannot quietly persist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the webhook/rerun secret no longer appears in any log record the receiver emits, proven by
      a test that asserts on the emitted log line with a sentinel value and is verified RED by
      reverting the fix.
- [ ] the mechanism is stated in the code where the choice is made (header vs redaction filter),
      including WHY — so a future change does not reintroduce the query-string form as a
      convenience.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`'s `/rerun` recipe no longer instructs the operator to
      put the token in a URL, and carries a note that the previous token must be treated as
      compromised and rotated.
- [ ] the access log still records route and status for both endpoints (the observability greps
      and debugging value are not sacrificed to fix this).
- [ ] ROTATION IS TRACKED SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY: the currently-logged token is rotated, and
      that rotation is recorded as done rather than assumed, since the code fix does not
      un-leak what is already in journald.
data.title: Review-bot logs the webhook token in plaintext on every /webhook and /rerun request
